title: With BorderlessMaximizedWindows turned on, allow dragging maximized window from empty space in top Panel
line: Dragging the empty space of a top panel now pulls the maximized window below it out of maximization and moves it, as if dragging its titlebar.
explanation: Nothing in the panel reacted to a drag on its empty space, so with borderless maximized windows a top panel left no place to grab the window from. The panel containment now has a DragHandler that, when a left-button drag starts on empty space (no applet, or a panel spacer) of a top panel, asks the window manager to move the active window of that screen if it is maximized (libtaskmanager requestMove). KWin handled that request by warping the pointer to the window's centre, so the restored window was held by its middle; when a button is held, KWin now grabs the window by its top edge under the pointer instead, so the titlebar follows the cursor. Because KWin then owns the pointer, the panel never gets the button release; it calls startSystemMove() on its own window, which makes Qt release the button (as Qt does for its own system moves) and does nothing to the layer-shell panel, otherwise the next drag on the panel was swallowed.

commits.message:
containments/panel: drag maximized windows from empty top panel space

With borderless maximized windows there is no titlebar to grab, and
dragging the empty space of a top panel did nothing. Now it starts
moving the maximized active window on that screen, like its titlebar.

BUG: 433072

window: don't warp the pointer for move requests during a drag

A move requested through plasma-window-management always warped the
pointer to the window's center, so a drag from a panel grabbed the
window in the middle. With a button held, grab its top edge instead.

BUG: 433072

media.caption: Top panel, Konsole maximized with BorderlessMaximizedWindows: dragging down from the empty part of the panel does nothing
Same drag with the fix: the window unmaximizes and follows the cursor by its titlebar; after re-maximizing, a second drag works too
Mid-drag (button held, cursor at 840,350) on master: the window stays maximized
Mid-drag with the fix: the window is restored with its titlebar under the cursor
